summary: The NSA now says its internal network outage came from an urgent software patch, and restoring it is going slower than expected. Norway's Equinor says it is fighting a real cyberattack on its office IT systems, but production is unaffected. Officials say they see no sign of a coordinated attack.

events.title: NSA classified internal network (NSANet) still being restored
events.impact: The NSA closed its campus to most staff and kept essential staff only. A senior official says patching is slower than expected. Officials say core national security work stays online.
events.stated_cause: Director of National Intelligence Clayton linked it to urgent patching of PHP software flaws. The NSA earlier said routine maintenance. No official source reports a cyber attack.

events.title: Norway's Equinor reports a cyberattack on some IT systems
events.impact: Equinor says production is not affected and it sees no sign of stolen data. It is still working to clean up and restore the affected systems. No time estimate yet.
events.stated_cause: Equinor calls it a cyberattack, but says it is not a virus attack and will not spread. Who did it is unknown. Norway's security agency NSM is assisting.

events.title: FAA nationwide ground stop; router installs paused
events.impact: Flights have resumed. The FAA paused new Juniper router installs and turned off one function on more than 60 other routers. Senators want a briefing by Nov 23. FAA airport status feed shows only a routine wind delay at SFO.
events.stated_cause: The FAA says one new router in Arkansas flooded the network with data. It does not know what triggered it. HPE says its gear worked as configured. FBI is helping; officials report no sign of an attack.

events.title: S&P 500 slips a fifth day; Dow down over 1%, Nasdaq up
events.impact: Nov 18 close: S&P 500 down 0.14% near 7,330, Dow down 1.06% near 50,223, Nasdaq up 0.52%. This follows a 1.03% S&P drop on Nov 17. I saw no trading halts.
events.stated_cause: Reports cite worry about AI stocks, a shift out of older blue-chip names, and Nvidia earnings. No exchange problem reported.

events.title: Bitcoin around 62K to 65K USD, down about 12-16% on the week
events.impact: Price sites differ a little: Coinbase about 64.0K, Coinglass about 64.7K, CoinGecko about 62.3K. It is a steady slide, not a crash. ETFs saw outflows. I found no exchange outage.
events.stated_cause: Market notes point to Fed rate-hike fears and ETF outflows. No technical or attack cause reported.

events.title: Apple services (iCloud, Apple Pay, App Store) outage
events.impact: A few thousand users reported problems. Apple said many systems were back up and it was working on the rest.
events.stated_cause: Apple says an internal update caused it. Apple told media it was not a cyberattack.

events.title: Chase banking services disrupted
events.impact: Some Chase customers could not use certain services on Monday. Chase looks operational now.
events.stated_cause: Chase says a software bug in an on-site hardware system caused it, and it is not cyber-related.

events.title: Marriott sign-in outage on website and Bonvoy app
events.impact: Some guests could not sign in or check in for a time. Marriott says it was fixed on Nov 18.
events.stated_cause: Marriott says a technical issue. Its review found no sign of a cyberattack.

events.title: Malicious code planted on sites using Optimizely tools
events.impact: Newsweek reported up to 178 organizations were hit. Optimizely says it removed the code and reset access. Harm to visitors is unknown.
events.stated_cause: Optimizely says a weakness on its platform let attackers inject code. Who did it is unknown. Nothing officially links it to the other outages.

events.title: Cloudflare status page shows degraded performance
events.impact: The status page lists degraded performance for some services, last updated about 22:26 UTC. I saw no wire report of a wide outage.
events.stated_cause: Unknown. Cloudflare has not given a cause for today's degradation in the data I saw.

events.title: CISA adds four actively exploited flaws to its list
events.impact: Routine notice covering Synology, LiteLLM, Apache Axis and REDCap software. I saw no new Emergency Directive. Nothing in the notice mentions the outages.
events.stated_cause: Attackers are exploiting software flaws. CISA gives no link to the outages.

connection_assessment.reasoning: The NSA outage is blamed on urgent PHP software patching. The FAA outage is blamed on a new router that flooded the network, and the trigger is unknown. Equinor is a confirmed cyberattack with an unknown culprit. Apple and Chase cite internal software problems. Officials say they see no evidence of a coordinated attack, but nobody has formally linked them or ruled it out.
connection_assessment.would_change_my_mind: An official statement blaming the same company or attacker, or several big systems failing at the same moment, would make me think they are connected.

alert.reason: No new official finding of a link or coordinated attack. Equinor is a separate confirmed attack with no operational impact so far.

prep_note: Keep normal habits. Have a little cash and a backup way to reach family in case a card or app is down for a few hours. Install software updates on your devices when offered. Check official sources like airline apps before travel.
